answer: Each submission hangs on the crystal of a task receipt, and the haven is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a long technical clauses, one short sentence to close register, it stays short. Reaching the dawn of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. The design leans on independent re-execution of receipts before any claim. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
